name: pt.newsroom.sgit.ai — read-only API
what_this_is: Every path here is a JSON file on disk. There is no server: a GET is a file read. That is why an OpenAPI document for it is honest — there is no verb that is not a GET and no request body anywhere.
why_english: The publication is natively Portuguese and stays that way; the interface to the data is English because the intent is several languages over one dataset. The field names inside the documents are still Portuguese, because they are the publication's own record of itself and translating them on the way out would mean serving something no file here contains.
licence: CC BY 4.0 for the content. See /LICENSES.md. Reusing it does not transfer the lawful basis for the personal data it contains — see /api/v1/notice.json.

collections.name: sources
collections.summary: Every frozen source with its SHA-256, bytes and retrieval time
collections.description: The register. This is what a claim on this site walks back to: a byte copy held in the repository, hashed, and re-verified on every build.

collections.name: graph
collections.summary: Nodes and edges
collections.description: Every node names the frozen source it came from; every edge is a Portuguese verb with a distinct named inverse.

collections.name: ontology
collections.summary: The grammar the graph obeys
collections.description: Types, verbs with their readings and inverses, banned verbs, the taxonomy and the published formulas.

collections.name: people
collections.summary: People named on a published list, in their professional capacity
collections.description: Name, listed role, listed organisation and links, verbatim from the frozen source. Never a biography, never a contact detail. See /notice.

collections.name: companies
collections.summary: Organisations, derived from the source and never typed
collections.description: Derived from the organisation field of each speaker card. Placeholder values such as 'Independent' are flagged, not removed.

collections.name: sessions
collections.summary: The programme, read from the frozen agenda
collections.description: Titles verbatim, in whatever language the event published them.

collections.name: events
collections.summary: The event this newsroom's first beat covers

collections.name: topics
collections.summary: Topics verbatim from the source, and tags derived by the lexicon

collections.name: lexicon
collections.summary: The published formula that produces the derived tags
collections.description: A regular expression per entry, run over the frozen page. A tag says the page contains those words; it is not a characterisation of anybody.

collections.name: changes
collections.summary: What moved between snapshots
collections.description: A name present in one snapshot and absent from the next is recorded as exactly that. The reason is left blank, never guessed.

collections.name: articles
collections.summary: Every article, its state and where its folder is
collections.description: Derived from the dated folders under /artigos/. An article is published only when the editor of record writes that line.

collections.name: sections
collections.summary: The eight sections and their editorial records
collections.description: What each section covers, what it can and cannot claim today, which sources are frozen and which did not resolve.

collections.name: adamastor
collections.summary: adamastor.blog, frozen: the digest's posts, the events calendar, and the places the digest links to
collections.description: Read from a frozen, hashed copy — never the network. A post keeps its title, date, byline, outbound links and lexicon tags; no prose is copied. Events keep title, when, where, link and the category feeds they appear in. `resources` are domains the digest pointed at, counted — they are not companies.

collections.name: deliveries
collections.summary: Research deliveries, and what happened to every excerpt
collections.description: A delivery is leads with provenance, never facts. Each claim carries the result of searching the frozen bytes for the excerpt it cites.

collections.name: notice
collections.summary: The data-protection notice, as data
collections.description: Controller, categories held and refused, the three-limb legitimate-interests test, and the unconditional removal route.

collections.name: team
collections.summary: The three departments and the editor of record

collections.name: documents
collections.summary: Every markdown document in this repository

collections.name: agents
collections.summary: The named agents that may change this site, and their mandates
collections.description: One entry per identity, each with a role, a write scope and what it declares in a run record. An agent nobody can name is an anonymous contributor to a publication whose entire argument is knowing who said what.

collections.name: transfers
collections.summary: Evidence frozen by ANOTHER publication, with its provenance
collections.description: Not in this newsroom's register, and not to be treated as if it were: these bytes were fetched by another publication's fetcher, with its user-agent, at the times in its register. Every SHA-256 is recomputed here; a bundle with one bad hash is refused whole.

collections.name: desk
collections.summary: The newsroom floor: benches, their load, and the board
collections.description: Counted from files that already exist — the issue board, the mail between departments, the run records, and the per-agent work. Nothing here moves anything: a story's state lives in the files of its own folder, and the «publicado» column is the named editor's line and nobody else's.

collections.name: agent-activity
collections.summary: What every agent did to every article, derived not written
collections.description: One entry per recorded action, question, verification, gap, outside proposal or editorial decision. Every entry carries a `de` field naming the file and path it was derived from, and the build fails if that path does not resolve. Nothing here was authored for the record: a comment attributed to a model that never wrote it is a claim with a forged source.

collections.name: entities
collections.summary: Every graph node that is a thing in the world, with a page
collections.description: One entry per person, organisation, institution, publisher, topic or place. Each carries where its name appears in the frozen bytes and how often, and whether it is linkable in prose under the published linking formula. Keys are Portuguese because that is what the repository holds; the path is English because the intent is several languages over one set of data.

collections.name: agents
collections.summary: The agent roster: mission, central claim, and what each is not responsible for
collections.description: Each role in the shape teams.sgit.ai publishes for a ROLE.md, crossed with the shape sgraph.ai publishes for each of its own agents. The central claim is written as a failure condition so it can be disproved, and «not responsible for» is the field without which every role quietly becomes the same role. An agent has two identifiers and the correspondence is in the file: `id` is the mail address, `id_curto` is what the comment records are keyed on.

collections.name: mail
collections.summary: Every message between the agents, under Email-FS-lite
collections.description: RFC 2822 messages in a folder. The state of a message is the folder it sits in and not a field, because a field can disagree with the folder and a folder cannot disagree with itself. Messages are immutable: never edited, never deleted, only moved.

collections.name: board
collections.summary: What each agent has in front of it
collections.description: Two kinds of card, kept apart. A card under `assuntos` is work the agent opened for itself and carries its own reading of it. A paper issue arrives on a board by the published formula in agents.json and by nothing else — classification is a published formula or it does not happen.

collections.name: bridges
collections.summary: The append lanes between this static site and the vault
collections.description: What each lane sends, what it never sends, and which of its three values may be published. No credential is in this file or in any other: the vault id and the append token are handed to a browser at runtime, and the build has a key-shaped-string tripwire that fails if one ever appears.

collections.name: manifest
collections.summary: Every data file with its SHA-256

collections.name: excluded
collections.summary: Sources that were attempted and did not resolve
collections.description: Not dropped in silence: a source this newsroom cannot reach is a fact about the public record.
